properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued August 29 at 1:55AM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Waters from Little River Inlet SC to South Santee River SC from 20
to 60 NM...

At 155 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a strong thunderstorm, capable
of producing winds to around 30 knots. This thunderstorm was located
19 nm south of Sunset Mid Shelf Buoy, moving northeast at 5 knots.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until this storm passes. If caught on the open water,
prepare for deteriorating conditions. Make sure you and your crew are
wearing properly fitted life jackets.

This storm may produce a waterspout. A Special Marine Warning may be
needed.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Southeastern Davis County in northern Utah...

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

imminent.

thunderstorms. Overflowing poor drainage areas will cause minor
flooding in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 0.75 inches of
rain have fallen.

the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.

Bountiful, Farmington, North Salt Lake, Centerville, Woods Cross
and West Bountiful.

properties.description:

Western Cobb County in north central Georgia...
Northeastern Douglas County in north central Georgia...

heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain

possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Kennesaw State University and Mableton.

Westbrook Creek, Noonday Creek, Dry Creek, Ward Creek, Etowah
River, Nickajack Creek, Noses Creek, Sweetwater Creek, Butternut
Creek, Rottenwood Creek and Powder Springs Creek.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued August 28 at 9:31PM EDT until August 29 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Caribou ME
properties.description:
* WHAT...The warm air temperatures from the mid 70 to around 80
may cause people to underestimate the dangers of the cold water
temperatures which are currently in the 50 to 55 degree range.

* WHERE...Coastal Hancock and Coastal Washington Counties.

* WHEN...From 8 AM EDT Saturday through Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...The cold water temperatures can quickly cause
hypothermia to anyone immersed in the waters. Anyone on boats
or paddlecraft should use extreme caution to avoid this threat.
properties.instruction:
A Beach Hazards Statement is issued on days when a significant
number of boats and paddlecraft are expected to be out on the
water and when warm air temperatures may cause people to
underestimate the danger of the cold water. Paddle smart from the
start. Always wear your life jacket. Be aware of wind conditions,
tides, and localized currents.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 28 at 3:45PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Imperial County APCD has issued an air quality alert
due to harmful levels of particle pollution from windblown dust.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...Western Imperial County. Levels of particle pollution can
vary by time and location depending on emissions and local weather
conditions.

* WHEN...tonight through Saturday, Aug 29 2026.

* IMPACTS... Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and
cause serious health problems such as asthma attacks, heart and lung
disease symptoms, and increased risk of lung infections. Everyone
can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with lung or
heart disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

To help minimize outdoor particle pollution levels:

* Carpool, telecommute, reduce trips, or take public
transportation
* Slow down if driving on dirt roads
* Stabilize loose soils
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued August 28 at 9:17AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
ESFSJU

The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical Storm
Dolly, located nearly 1200 miles southeast of the local islands. The
official forecast calls for Dolly to degenerate into a tropical wave
before reaching the area on Sunday and Monday.

Since the system is expected to find a hostile environment, a
widespread and long-lasting rainfall event is not anticipated.
Instead, squally weather will bring periods of moderate to locally
heavy rainfall, beginning late Sunday and stretching into Monday. In
general, we are anticipating rainfall accumulations of 1 to 3 inches,
which will be beneficial for any areas receiving the rain. Lingering
moisture from the remnants of Dolly could contribute to additional
showers developing on Tuesday. The risk of flooding is low to locally
medium. Areas with the drainage system clogged by death vegetation
debris or urbanized areas with poor drainage could experience
localized flooding.

Any rainfall will be welcome, and could bring a temporary relieve to
the ongoing severe to extreme drought plaguing Puerto Rico and the
Virgin Islands. However, the rain should not be enough to end the
drought.

At this time, the confidence in the forecast is medium, and the users
are advised to monitor the forecast in case changes are introduced.
If that the case, this product will be update accordingly.
